verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same three formulas, up to two routine rewritings. (i) Sign convention: Lean's `signedAxialLoop` is −b_L (its own docstring says so) and its φ-mean is `a p * m p` = −b_s = −b_0; with c = −E/2 the stated derivative E·(−signedAxialLoop + a·m)/2 is E₀(b_L − b_0)/2, the paper's ½E₀(b_L − b₀). The angular case is literal: c = −1/2, mean a = a_0, derivative −(a_L − a_0)/2. (ii) Localization: Lean defines the primitives as a cutoff times the zero-mean primitive (`extendedPrimitive χ f m c (p,θ) = χ.value p * normalizedPrimitiveFamily …`), so the two derivative identities are stated for p ∈ K, where χ = 1; the paper likewise asserts them on ℐ × [−1,1] and extends by zero off ℐ, justifying the extension by the loop being constant near ∂ℐ (the Lean analogue of that vanishing is `boundary_vanishing`, ParametricModulation.lean:416). The zero-mean clause holds in Lean for every p, with no restriction. The parameter p ranges over (X,η), as in the paper.
